desc.concept: Auxiliary/copula verbs (be, were, was, is) in passive or stative clauses
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly forms of be (were, be, is, being, was, will be); the remaining windows are scattered unrelated tokens with no shared feature.

desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous (the, ting, do, of, power, windows, liquid, goods, on, processing, nder, out, marijuana, naked, for, Japan, alcohol, continuously, Nation, receive); windows span unrelated domains, so no single concept fits.

desc.note: Marked tokens are varied: suffixes (-s, /s), fragments (Ins, S, ph, reg), articles (the, a), and possessives (their). No single concept covers the windows.

desc.concept: mixed scientific prose tokens, no shared feature
desc.note: The marked tokens (R, -ray, as, by, -sensitive, low, this, using, C, and, ers, broad, range, larger) are unrelated function words and fragments with no common concept; the windows are scientific text from varied fields.

desc.concept: markup/code tokens inside HTML, XML, CSS, LaTeX code snippets
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous (input, button, option, indentation whitespace, tags); the shared trait is that each window is source code or markup, not a single token type.

desc.concept: scattered tokens within unrelated subword or name fragments; no shared concept
desc.note: Marked tokens span ten unrelated features (brand names, LaTeX brackets, medical terms, nouns); no single concept covers 25% of windows.

desc.concept: quantity/number words in numeric or quantifier phrases
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly prepositions/determiners (per, each, of, next) and number fragments (3, 0, 2, five, two); the unit fires on positions inside quantity phrases, not one specific token.

desc.concept: mathematical or code operators such as '=', '<', '-', '+' in formulas
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous operator symbols across math LaTeX, code and HTML; no single concept covers 25%+ of windows cleanly.

desc.concept: mixed fragments inside names and closing tags; no single feature
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous (name fragments like ier/ov/aur/ur/ill, and the ">" closing-bracket token in HTML/XML). No shared concept covers a majority of windows.

desc.concept: mixed unrelated tokens; no shared feature
